recommendation: Treat certified seeds with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg or Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg seed before wet nursery sowing. For dry nursery, ensure 10 cents nursery area per acre.
relevance_reason: Prevents seed-borne seedling blight and early blast infection while promoting root elongation in nursery beds.
supporting_source: TNAU Agritech Portal — Paddy Crop Production Guide (Wet Seedbed Management)
limitations_disclaimer: Seed treatment protocol depends on variety and seed moisture level. Contact Block Agricultural Extension Officer if seedlings show root rot or yellowing.

recommendation: Adopt Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) irrigation: allow water to drop 2-5 cm below soil surface before re-irrigating to 2-3 cm depth.
relevance_reason: Saves up to 25-30% irrigation water, improves soil aeration, strengthens root anchoring, and mitigates methane emissions.
supporting_source: TNAU Water Technology Centre & IRRI Guidelines on AWD
limitations_disclaimer: Do not practice AWD during flowering/panicle initiation stage where continuous thin film (2 cm) of water is mandatory.

recommendation: Monitor for yellow stem borer and leaf folder. Set up 4 light traps or 5 pheromone traps per acre. If leaf folder damage exceeds 10% ETL (Economic Threshold Level), spray neem oil 3% (30 ml/L) or botanical extract.
relevance_reason: Flowering stage is critical for panicle development. Unchecked stem borer causes dead hearts or white ears.
supporting_source: TNAU Department of Agricultural Entomology / ICAR-IIRR Guidelines
limitations_disclaimer: Verify ETL count before spraying any chemical insecticide. Avoid spraying during midday pollinating hours (10 AM - 12 PM).

recommendation: Drain standing water from the field 10 to 12 days before the intended harvest date. Harvest when 80-85% of grains in the panicle turn golden yellow.
relevance_reason: Allows uniform ripening, facilitates combine harvester movement, and prevents grain shattering or mould growth.
limitations_disclaimer: If unseasonal rainfall is forecasted, delay field draining and secure paddy sheaves on elevated drying platforms.

recommendation: Apply 50% nitrogen along with full dose of phosphorus and potassium as basal. Side-dress remaining nitrogen in two equal splits at square formation and peak flowering stages along with earthing up.
relevance_reason: Balanced split nutrition prevents excessive vegetative lankiness and enhances boll retention capacity.
supporting_source: ICAR-CICR (Central Institute for Cotton Research) Regional Station, Coimbatore
limitations_disclaimer: Dose must be tailored to soil test values (STCR). Excessive nitrogen during rainy cloudy days attracts sucking pests.

recommendation: Scout for pink bollworm (PBW) larvae and sucking pests (jassids, aphids, thrips). Install 5 pheromone traps per acre with Gossyplure septa. Use yellow sticky traps (10/acre) for whiteflies.
relevance_reason: Early detection in rosette flowers prevents internal boll damage where spray chemicals cannot penetrate.
supporting_source: TNAU Agritech Entomology & National Food Security Mission (Cotton)
limitations_disclaimer: Do not mix synthetic pyrethroids unnecessarily as this induces secondary pest resurgence. Consult KVK specialists if boll drop exceeds 15%.

recommendation: Provide propping with bamboo or casuarina poles against wind lodging. Apply SOP (Sulphate of Potash) @ 50g per plant after shooting, and denavel (remove male bud) after last hand opens.
relevance_reason: Denaveling diverts nutrients directly into developing fruit fingers, increasing bunch weight by 10-15%.
supporting_source: ICAR-NRCB (National Research Centre for Banana), Tiruchirappalli
limitations_disclaimer: Ensure propping is securely tied at two junctions before monsoon gusty winds. Avoid excessive chemical potash during soil drought.

recommendation: Broadcast Gypsum @ 200 kg/acre at 40-45 days after sowing (DAS) around root zones during earthing up, followed by light irrigation.
relevance_reason: Calcium is directly absorbed by developing pegs for shell hardening and kernel filling; avoids 'pops' (empty pods).
limitations_disclaimer: Do not disturb soil once peg penetration is underway (after 50 DAS) as it severs developing gynophores.

recommendation: Watch for early blight (concentric leaf rings) and leaf miner. Spray 1% Bordeaux mixture or Trichoderma harzianum as protective measure. Stake plants using trellises to avoid fruit ground contact.
relevance_reason: Staking elevates vines, improving solar interception and reducing fungal splash from soil pathogens during rain.
supporting_source: ICAR-IIHR (Indian Institute of Horticultural Research) Bengaluru / TNAU HC&RI
limitations_disclaimer: In case of severe viral leaf curl transmission by whiteflies, immediately rogue out infected plants. Consult district horticulture officer.

recommendation: Open circular basins of 1.8m radius around the palm trunk and apply coconut coir pith mulch (5 cm layer). In drip systems, deliver 55-65 litres of water per palm per day during dry months.
relevance_reason: Coir pith retains soil moisture, prevents root dehydration, and cushions microbial activity against heat waves.
supporting_source: Coconut Development Board (CDB) & TNAU Coconut Research Station, Veppankulam
limitations_disclaimer: Keep mulch 15 cm away from the base of the bole to avoid fungus collar rot. Clean crown before northeast monsoon.

recommendation: When weather forecasts indicate rainfall exceeding 25mm in 24 hours, clear field drainage channels immediately, suspend fertilizer top-dressing, and halt chemical spray applications.
relevance_reason: Prevents nutrient leaching, chemical runoff into water bodies, and waterlogging-induced root asphyxiation.
supporting_source: IMD (India Meteorological Department) & TNAU Agro Climate Research Centre
limitations_disclaimer: Local microtopography significantly affects ponding. Ensure tail-end drainage to avoid backflow.

recommendation: Incorporate green manure crops (Daincha / Sunnhemp @ 20 kg/ha) into the soil 45 days before sowing, or apply 5 tonnes of well-decomposed FYM (Farmyard Manure) per acre.
relevance_reason: Rebuilds depleted organic carbon (SOC), fosters beneficial mycorrhiza, and increases soil water holding capacity by up to 20%.
supporting_source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soil Science & TNAU Soil Science Dept
limitations_disclaimer: Allow at least 10 days for green manure decomposition before main crop transplanting to avoid anaerobic seedling damage.
